title: Reach the date with a keyboard
goal: A customer who uses only the keyboard books the 09:00 slot on a chosen date, and the booking is saved and reopens with that exact date.

steps.headline: Keyboard user got stuck at the date step: there is no date field to Tab to

steps.diagnosis: The date picker is rendered as a non-focusable div, preventing keyboard users from focusing the date field. Changing it to a readonly input makes it focusable while preserving the flatpickr UI.

edits.new: <input type="text" id="select-date" class="form-control mx-auto my-4" readonly>

steps.headline: Keyboard user got stuck: the expected control never appeared

steps.diagnosis: The date picker does not accept manual keyboard input because flatpickr's allowInput option is false, so typing a date and pressing Enter does not change the selected date, leaving no available hours to load.

steps.headline: Keyboard user got stuck at the date step: there is no date field to Tab to

steps.diagnosis: The date field is rendered as a non‑focusable div, so keyboard users cannot focus it and manual date entry is ignored because flatpickr lacks allowInput. Changing it to a focusable input and enabling allowInput lets users type a date and have it accepted.

steps.headline: Confirmation shown, but saved for 2026-11-01 09:00 instead of 2026-11-02 09:00

evidence.error: Outcome verification failed: wrong_start_datetime, wrong_end_datetime_or_duration, reopen_date_mismatch

timeline_after_typing_date.event: no key pressed (page changed it) → date field shows "01/11/2026"

steps.diagnosis: The date picker returns dates in the browser's timezone (UTC), but the server expects dates in the business timezone (Asia/Riyadh). When the user types a date in DD/MM/YYYY format, it is interpreted as UTC midnight, which corresponds to a different local date in Riyadh, causing the stored appointment to shift by one day. Converting the selected date to the business timezone before sending to the server fixes the mismatch.

The date picker defaults to interpreting manually entered dates as MM/DD/YYYY (en_US) while the verifier types DD/MM/YYYY, causing the selected date to be off by one month/day. Setting dateFormat to 'd/m/Y' makes flatpickr parse DD/MM/YYYY correctly, and adding allowInput permits manual entry.

steps.diagnosis: The date field was non‑focusable and flatpickr lacked allowInput and proper date format parsing, causing manual DD/MM/YYYY entry to be ignored or misinterpreted. Changing the field to an input, enabling allowInput, setting dateFormat to 'd/m/Y', and converting selected dates to the business timezone (Asia/Riyadh) ensures keyboard entry yields the correct date.
